I wrote the test spec for REQ-001 in `aiws/work/REQ-001/03-test-spec.md`, which is the only file I changed. It has 43 test cases: 32 BE and 11 FE. Every acceptance criterion from AC-1 to AC-22 has at least one test case, and no test case points to an AC that doesn't exist. I couldn't run the orchestrator's parser because Bash was denied. Instead I checked the file by search: IDs run TC-1..TC-43 with no gaps, each has exactly one `covers` line and one `side` line (`be`/`fe`), and I cross-checked the AC table by hand. The orchestrator's own validation at commit is still the check that counts.

**How the test cases split across files.** Each test case lives in exactly one test file, in blocks that follow the design's task groups:

| Test cases | Test file | Group |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TC-1..TC-10 | `PhoneNumbersTest.java` (new) | BE-1 |
| TC-11..TC-12 | `InMemoryCustomerRepositoryTest.java` (new) | BE-2 |
| TC-13..TC-26 | `CustomerServiceTest.java` | BE-3 |
| TC-27..TC-32 | `CustomerHandlerTest.java` | BE-3 |
| TC-33..TC-35 | `formatPhone.test.js` (new) | FE-1 |
| TC-36..TC-41 | `customerTable.test.js` | FE-1 |
| TC-42..TC-43 | `customerApi.test.js` | FE-2 |

**Key decisions**
- **Test design techniques:**
  - equivalence partitions for the phone input;
  - boundary values (lengths 9–12, `84` followed by 10/11/12 characters, `"+84"` on its own);
  - a decision table for the duplicate-number rule (BR-09);
  - named cases for the wrong implementations the design warns about: `String.trim()`/`strip()`, a regex ending in `$`, Unicode whitespace classes, `find()` instead of `matches()`, the null-pointer case `c.phone().equals(...)`, and escaping HTML before formatting.
- **Catching the null-pointer case:** every service and HTTP test that checks duplicates or saves a valid number runs with an active customer that has no phone already in the store.
- **Rejection tests:** they use a valid, unused name and email, so the only error is `phone`. They check the exact message and that the customer count doesn't change.
- **Test levels:** TC-27..TC-32 are labelled `integration`. They start the server in-process on a random port (`App.start(0)`) inside `be_test`, so they need no outside environment. Everything else is `unit`.
- **No new dependency:** table-driven BE tests can use `@ParameterizedTest`, which is already included in the `junit-jupiter` dependency. The spec also notes the Java string-escape pitfalls for control characters.

**Things the reviewer and planner must know**
- **The planner must include the two "optional" test files.** The design marked `InMemoryCustomerRepositoryTest.java` and `formatPhone.test.js` as optional, but this spec uses them. They must go into BE-2 and FE-1. Otherwise TC-11..TC-12 and TC-33..TC-35 fail the check that each test case appears in the test files its task changes.
- **Some test data rests on an unconfirmed assumption carried over from the design.** Rows in TC-2, 3, 6, 10, 13, 17 and 21 assume the legacy server strips a vertical tab in the middle of a number but keeps non-breaking and em spaces. They are marked `[CẦN XÁC NHẬN]` (needs confirmation). If the legacy server behaves differently, those rows must change.
- **No HTTP test for AC-13 on purpose.** TC-26 covers it at service level, and TC-29/TC-30 show that validation errors reach the HTTP response in the standard error format.
- **The page form and submit handler (`index.html`, `main.js`) have no unit tests,** because `node:test` has no DOM. The analysis already says to check them by review or by running the app.
